clue.text: Jostle the Spanish crook

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
to crook an arm or finger is to bend or bow it

explanation.surface: Someone shoves a bent Spaniard out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push or shove them with your arm, which is what jostling means.

clue.text: English get nicer stews full of beans

indicators.note: stews means the letters of get nicer are cooked up and stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: English cooking improves its casseroles, which become hearty.
explanation.walkthrough: Full of beans looks like a description of stew, but it is the idiom for lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of beans is an idiom for lively and vigorous, brimming with energy.

clue.text: Revealed bust

definitions.meaning: second meaning: having no money, bankrupt

explanation.definitionFit: Broke is the past tense of break, as in disclosing news, and also an adjective for penniless.

clue.text: American painter's short pipe

indicators.note: short means the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter

explanation.surface: An artist from the US owns a stubby tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is a simple wind instrument, a small pipe you blow into.

clue.text: Shocks gentleman with awards, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase before is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: a gentleman is addressed as sir, and awards are prizes: said together they sound like the answer

explanation.surface: A decorated knight's honours come as a jolt to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprises as a verb means startles or catches unawares, the same as shocks.

clue.text: Watch son coming onto the stage

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
an actor's entry is their coming onto the stage

explanation.surface: A parent keeps an eye on their boy as he walks onstage.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a guard on duty, the role of a sentry posted to keep lookout.

clue.text: Made public embarrassed about rent

indicators.note: about means the embarrassed word goes around the rent word

parts.note: red in the face, so embarrassed
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A red-faced tenant announced the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Released news or records have been issued and so made available to everyone.

clue.text: What patients hope to do? Put up hospital department shelter

indicators.note: Put up in a down clue raises the letters for the hospital department, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: ER is the emergency room
cover is shelter

explanation.surface: Patients wish the casualty ward would erect some shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients want to get better, to regain health after illness or injury.

clue.text: Work is nicest time for boffin

indicators.note: Work as a verb means the letters of is nicest are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A claim that the office is most pleasant at a particular hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: Watched broadcast — section of Hamlet?

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard rather than read, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: seen means watched

explanation.surface: A TV showing of Shakespeare's play is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet might be a small village, but here it is the play, divided into acts and scenes; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A play like Hamlet is divided into acts and these shorter units of action.

clue.text: Gushing movement in each lake

indicators.note: in places the movement word inside the letters for each and lake

parts.note: a motion is a movement
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Water rushes and swirls within every lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushing describes effusive, overflowing feeling, which is being emotional.

clue.text: Lecture companion that is pinching diamonds

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: pinching means the letters for that is close around the diamonds letter

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A friend caught stealing jewels gets a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone is to scold or reprove them at length, as chiding does.

clue.text: One might admit you agree terms to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A negotiator concedes that the conditions are acceptable, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeter stands at the door of a shop or venue welcoming people and letting them in.

clue.text: Suggest a very boring trip

indicators.note: boring means the very letter drills into the trip word

parts.note: to trip, as in trip the light fantastic, is to dance

explanation.surface: Someone proposes an outing that sounds extremely tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance an idea or theory is to put it forward, propose or suggest it.

clue.text: Tons requested to be burdened with work

parts.note: asked means requested

explanation.surface: Someone asked for heavy loads and is now weighed down with jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tasked is to have been assigned duties, loaded with jobs to do.

clue.text: I seem most agitated on occasion

indicators.note: agitated means the letters of I seem most are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they appear most anxious every now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: On occasion means now and then, not always, which is what sometimes means.

clue.text: Student justifying what he is doing?

parts.note: L is the learner plate, so a student or learner
earning your keep is justifying it, deserving what you get

explanation.surface: A pupil defends his conduct, prompting the question of what exactly he is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the student in the clue: a student is, after all, studying.
explanation.definitionFit: A student's whole activity is acquiring knowledge, so studying is what he is doing.

clue.text: Prowess shown by bighead after split

parts.note: great means big
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: An arrogant person's ability shows once the group breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split bighead into big and head, then translate each half.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is outstanding skill or ability, a mark of distinction.

clue.text: Record finished after daughter rested

indicators.note: after places the record and finished words behind the daughter letter

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
an EP is an extended-play record
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A girl took a break once her recording was complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on something is to rest or rely on it, as an argument rests on evidence.

clue.text: Contrasted flipping old Conservative politician with a socialist

indicators.note: flipping turns the letters for old Conservative back to front

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A party-switching Tory MP is set against a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare two things is to set them side by side to weigh their differences, which is contrasting them.

clue.text: Review any ales drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of any ales are tipsily jumbled

explanation.surface: A beer critic assesses whatever beers have been sampled.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to examine it in detail, to review it closely.

clue.text: Lowers cold beer, with teetotaller entering

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: entering means the teetotaller letters go inside the beer word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal or a teetotaller

explanation.surface: A man downs a chilled beer while a non-drinker walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowers is not about bringing something down: read it as low-ers, things that moo.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows low, or moo, so cattle are lowers in this crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Hesitated, topless, getting changed

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: faltered means hesitated or wavered

explanation.surface: Someone paused nervously before stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered means modified or made different, which is what changed means.

clue.text: Left section with editor

parts.note: a part is a section

explanation.surface: A section went out together with its editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Parted can mean went away or departed, as in parted company, so left.

clue.text: About to get a new house

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: new signals the words to get a are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is on the verge of buying a brand-new home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the countryside.

clue.text: Was concerned about cutting scoundrel

indicators.note: cutting means the about letters slice into the scoundrel word

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a villain getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cared means felt worry or interest, being concerned about someone.

clue.text: Go angling twice initially with lure

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of angling and of twice

parts.note: to lure is to tempt

explanation.surface: A fisherman has a second try with bait.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is a try or an attempt, as in have a go.

clue.text: One enters considerably damp

indicators.note: enters means the One letter goes into the considerably word

parts.note: most means very or considerably, as in most kind
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone walks in soaking wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, which is damp.

clue.text: After drink, fancy that card game

indicators.note: After puts the fancy that word following the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
my! is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy that!

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise after a drink and proposes a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game where players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: Put off by my own influence

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
mine means belonging to me, my own

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged by the force of their own personality.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine an outcome is to shape or decide it, which is to influence it.

clue.text: Stooped, but no convict fell

indicators.note: but no says the convict word is taken out of the stooping word

parts.note: to stoop to something is to condescend
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A man bent down, though not a prisoner, then took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Stooped is the figurative sense, lowering oneself, which is condescended; remove CON to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Descended means came or went down, as something that fell did.

clue.text: Sees Democrat consumed small fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: goes out with romantically
second meaning: the sweet fruit of the date palm

parts.note: ate means consumed
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A politician spotted eating a little piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dates a person is seeing them; dates are also the fruit of a palm tree.
